ambiguities.text: No documentation on behavior when value length exceeds the specified size parameter
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume Python's rjust/ljust behavior: when value is longer than size, the original value is returned unmodified (no truncation). This needs verification against actual implementation.

ambiguities.text: No explicit bounds checking documented for the size parameter
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume calling code is responsible for ensuring size is within reasonable bounds. Memory exhaustion possible with extremely large size values.

implicit_assumptions.description: The size parameter is assumed to be a valid non-negative integer convertible via int()
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Invalid or negative size values could cause unexpected behavior or exceptions

implicit_assumptions.description: Sufficient memory is available to allocate the padded result
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Memory exhaustion if extremely large size values are passed

implicit_assumptions.description: Callers of these functions provide size values that make semantic sense for the byte data being processed
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Incorrect padding could lead to malformed data in EVM operations
